display_name: Report a session's own context-window occupancy snapshot
description: maintenance-verbs M1 (shape (a)). Overwrites the caller's single latest context-status snapshot — agent_instance_id, the Claude Code session_id it was measured against, the model, current_tokens (input + cache_creation + cache_read from the most recent assistant turn), the resolved per-model ceiling, and when it was measured. The caller (today: the rotation_due_watch.py hook, on every un-throttled tick) already did the local transcript read and the ceiling lookup — this verb trusts the reported values and performs a plain state upsert, no file or subprocess I/O of its own. One row per agent_instance_id, always overwritten, never a history. Also carries three OPTIONAL cache-state fields describing THE MOST RECENT ASSISTANT CALL — the same call current_tokens is summed from: cache_read_tokens (0 means that call read nothing from cache and paid full price), cache_cold, and cache_overage_signature. Omitting them records NOT REPORTED, which reads back as null rather than as a warm cache — a reporter that never looked and one that looked and found the cache live are different facts. cache_cold excludes the first call after a /clear, which is cold by construction because the clear rewrites the prefix. Also carries two OPTIONAL reporter-attribution fields saying WHICH COPY of the reporting hook produced the snapshot: reporter_surface, a path CLASS rather than a machine-specific path ('checkout' for a hook under the repo's own .claude/hooks including its subdirectories, 'plugin_cache' for an installed plugin-cache copy, 'vendored' for the in-repo source an install copies from, 'release' for that same source inside a deployed release tree, and 'unknown' when the hook cannot classify its own location — any other value is rejected outright), and reporter_generation, the hook's own content-generation counter, deliberately not a git commit sha because a hook cannot know the commit it was copied from. These exist because several copies of the reporting hook can be registered on the same event at once, they serialize on a shared throttle that records nothing about who claimed it, and this table keeps only the latest write — so without them a row cannot be attributed, and an absent cache field is indistinguishable from a stale copy having served that tick. Omitting them records a pre-attribution reporter, which is itself a positive finding about that row.
embedding_description: A session reporting its own context-window token usage, its model ceiling, whether its prompt cache is still live, and which copy of the reporting hook is speaking. Writes a measurement a hook already took from the transcript. Cache fields are optional; omitting them means not measured, which differs from measured-and-warm. An absent reporter identity marks a hook copy predating attribution.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: {"status": "recorded"} on success — the caller's latest snapshot row was overwritten.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Routine and high-frequency (every un-throttled hook tick); do not narrate a normal success, only surface a failure.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: A predicated upsert on session_context_status, conflicting on agent_instance_id alone (one row per session, always latest).
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: missing_argument: one of agent_instance_id/claude_session_id/model/measured_at was empty. negative_tokens: current_tokens or ceiling was non-positive, which cannot be a real measurement — the caller has a bug, not a transient fault. state_service_unavailable: the state service is not bound. unknown_reporter_surface: reporter_surface was not one of checkout/plugin_cache/vendored/release/unknown — an invented or typo'd surface would quietly poison the attribution these fields exist to provide, so it fails before any write rather than being stored.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: missing_argument and negative_tokens indicate the reporting hook computed or forwarded a bad value — fix the caller, do not retry the same call. state_service_unavailable is worth a retry once the platform is up. unknown_reporter_surface is likewise a caller bug: send 'unknown' when the hook cannot classify its own location — an admitted unknown is correct, an invented surface is not.
